items.title: Tesla's Robotaxi Fleet Might Finally Be Driving Around Austin Unsupervised
items.topic: Tesla's Robotaxi Fleet Might Finally Be Driving Around Austin Unsupervised
items.summary: Tesla's robotaxi fleet is reportedly operating unsupervised in Austin, marking a significant milestone in the deployment of autonomous vehicles. The company's Full Self-Driving (FSD) technology is being tested in real-world conditions, which could accelerate the commercialization of robotaxis. This deployment is crucial for validating the safety and reliability of Tesla's AV systems.

items.title: Nevada Opens The Door To Thousands Of Paid Robotaxis, And Tesla Has The Edge
items.topic: Nevada Opens The Door To Thousands Of Paid Robotaxis, And Tesla Has The Edge
items.summary: Nevada has approved Tesla, Uber, and Waymo to launch paid robotaxi services, potentially deploying thousands of autonomous vehicles. This regulatory green light is a major step forward for the commercialization of AVs, allowing these companies to test and refine their technologies in a real-world setting. The move could set a precedent for other states to follow.

items.title: Nevada Allows Uber, Tesla And Waymo To Start Paid Robotaxi Service
items.topic: Nevada Allows Uber, Tesla And Waymo To Start Paid Robotaxi Service
items.summary: Nevada has granted permission to Uber, Tesla, and Waymo to begin paid robotaxi services, paving the way for the widespread deployment of autonomous vehicles. This decision allows these companies to operate thousands of robotaxis, which will help them gather valuable data and improve their AV technologies. The move is expected to accelerate the adoption of autonomous ride-hailing services.

items.title: You can now ride a Chinese EV in the US as Waymo opens Zeekr Ojai to all
items.topic: You can now ride a Chinese EV in the US as Waymo opens Zeekr Ojai to all
items.summary: Waymo has opened its Zeekr Ojai robotaxis to the public in the United States, allowing riders to experience the Chinese EV in a fully autonomous setting. This deployment is part of Waymo's broader strategy to expand its robotaxi fleet and test the integration of different vehicle models into its autonomous driving system.

items.title: CommandLM: Data driven behavior level descriptor for ego vehicles
items.topic: CommandLM: Data driven behavior level descriptor for ego vehicles
items.summary: As autonomous driving systems move toward real-world deployment, interpretable, behavior-level decision-making is essential for safety, trust, and regulation. We introduce CommandLM, a multimodal large language model that generates concise, human-readable behavior descriptions for ego vehicles from fused multi-sensor data. Our model processes temporally fused bird's-eye view representations from LiDAR and multi-camera inputs via a Q-Former adapter connected to a quantized, LoRA-fine-tuned large language model.

items.title: Enhancement of Large Language Models Driving Knowledge for Practical Autonomous Driving Decision Making
items.topic: Enhancement of Large Language Models Driving Knowledge for Practical Autonomous Driving Decision Making
items.summary: Theoretical driving knowledge and hazard perception capability are essential for large language models (LLMs) to be qualified for driving or assisting autonomous vehicles. Our prior study found that the mainstream LLMs with relatively small size suitable for onboard or edge deployment failed driving theory tests. That raised several important research questions on application of LLMs for safety critical autonomous driving tasks: how to enhance the theoretical driving knowledge of LLMs and how to assess its impact on driving decision-making and safety in realistic scenarios.

items.title: Multi-Agent Orchestration with the Common-Sense Reasoning Capabilities of LLMs for Autonomous Driving
items.topic: Multi-Agent Orchestration with the Common-Sense Reasoning Capabilities of LLMs for Autonomous Driving
items.summary: Autonomous vehicles require robust perception and decision-making capabilities to operate in diverse and unseen scenarios. While reinforcement learning and rule-based methods can provide effective control and safety mechanisms, their performance may degrade in situations requiring contextual reasoning. Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in understanding multimodal information and generating contextual reasoning, however, their use for direct vehicle control can introduce latency and hallucination risks.
